response.title: which enclosed 3d printer heats up the fastest
response.answer:
For an enclosed FDM 3D printer, the fastest-heating model depends on what you want to heat:

Nozzle: How quickly it reaches 220–250°C for PLA or PETG.

Heated bed: How quickly it reaches 60°C for PLA or 100–110°C for ABS.

Enclosed chamber: How quickly the internal air reaches 50–65°C for ABS, ASA, or engineering materials.

If your goal is the shortest time from pressing Print to actually printing, nozzle and bed heating matter most. If you're printing ABS, ASA, or nylon, chamber heating can become the bottleneck.

Fastest chamber-heating candidates

Based on published warm-up figures, the QIDI Plus4 is one of the strongest documented contenders, although I couldn't verify a standardized head-to-head test establishing the overall fastest printer.
